Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Arsenal from Villa Park. The champions travel to the team that finished fourth last season in buoyant mood and form despite some misgivings within their fanbase about their recruitment this summer.

It amounts so far to making Pier Hincapié‘s loan into a proper transfer, revamping the left wing with Christos Tzolis replacing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, upgrading options in central midfield by buying Bruno Guimarães and selling Cristian Norgaard – and signing Ezri Konsa from today’s opponents to give them the greatest elite defensive depth that I can recall at club since Manchester City’s Treble winners had Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, John Stones, Nathan Aké, João Cancelo, Aymeric Laporte, Manuel Akanji, Rico Lewis and Sergio Gómez on the books at the same time.

Villa, by contrast, have endured a turbulent summer of trading with the departures of Europa League winners Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, the aforementioned Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martínez, raising, along with other departures, more than £315m. They have spent about £180m to remodel the team though Johan Manzambi, who is injured, and João Gomes, who is suspended after his red card in the 4-0 defeat by Brighton, are absent tonight.

We can expect to see Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri and hopefully Nicolas Jackson and Leon Goretzka who have been registered in time to play, plus the loan signings Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Alejandro Garnacho. Still to come are the pending purchases of Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye in a process that emphasises how profoundly Villa are invested in and dependent upon their manager, Unai Emery.

After so much upheaval, it would be foolish to set much store on Villa’s 2-1 victory last season, sealed by Emi Buendía’s winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time. Arsenal barely broke sweat in blowing Man City away in the Community Shield and cakewalked to victory over Coventry in the league’s opening fixture. His past work suggests Emery will be able to forge another formidable side from his talented new squad but this match feels two months too soon for him against his old club.

#1546. From Brasil: Roma inquire about Cruzeiro’s Kevin Arroyo

Roma are once again looking to Brazil to strengthen their attack.

After scouting him this summer, the Giallorossi have once again set their sights on Cruzeiro winger Kevin Arroyo.

As reported by Brazilian portal RTI Esporte, the 2006-born player is also facing competition from Benfica, who have long been eyeing the jewel in the crown at the Belo Horizonte club, having enjoyed a season with 8 goals and 8 assists in 50 appearances.

Cruzeiro’s asking price is high for Kevin Arroyo, valued by the Brazilians at a staggering €45 million.

The blue-and-white club has no intention of negotiating below this figure. Arroyo’s contract with Cruzeiro, which expires in December 2029, also includes a monstrous €100 million release clause, in addition to a 50% resale fee to Independiente del Valle.

#1544. French team: Zidane brought up Steve Ngoura

A nice surprise for Steve Ngoura. Summoned with the France Espoirs team for this November gathering, the Cercle Bruges striker had the opportunity to participate in the training of the France A team on Tuesday evening at Clairefontaine. The 21-year-old was called directly by Zinédine Zidane to temporarily join the French group, just 48 hours before traveling to Italy, as part of the Nations League. According to the journalist’s information Saber Desfargesthis invitation is explained by the withdrawal of Marcus Thuram, forced to leave the rally due to discomfort in his right hamstring. His replacement, Eli Junior Kroupi, having not yet arrived at Clairefontaine after a trip disrupted by London traffic jams, the French coach decided to call on Ngoura to complete his training squad.

This invitation represents a great reward for the former Le Havre striker, who has had an encouraging start to the season in Belgium. With four goals and two assists in the league under the colors of Cercle Bruges, Steve Ngoura stood out for his offensive performances, to the point of offering himself a first experience alongside the French internationals. Born in Ivry-sur-Seine, the young center forward does not, however, officially join the Blues group for the rest of the rally. His participation remains limited to this training session, organized to temporarily compensate for the lack of available players. A nevertheless precious opportunity for the 21-year-old player, who was able to discover the methods of Zinédine Zidane and measure himself against the executives of the France team.

#1543. Bologna expected to interrupt Dovbyk’s loan

Artem Dovbyk’s future could change as early as the January transfer window.

The Ukrainian striker, who joined Bologna on loan from Roma, has barely seen any playing time in the first half of the season, and the Rossoblu is considering ending his contract early.

As reported by Matteo Moretto on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, talks are expected between Roma and Bologna in the coming weeks to assess the striker’s situation.

The Emilian club is reportedly considering his departure, having developed concerns that Dovbyk isn’t the right striker for the team at this time, especially given the difficulties he’s encountered so far.

On the other hand, Roma hasn’t planned Dovbyk’s return in January.

The Giallorossi have in fact structured their annual sports program without considering the Ukrainian’s reinstatement mid-season.

Therefore, future discussions between the two clubs will clarify which solution to adopt ahead of the winter transfer window.

#1542. Michael Carrick facing the sack at Man United: Mauricio Pochettino the frontrunner to replace beleaguered boss - but chiefs face splashing out £7MILLION for former Spurs and Chelsea coach

Published: 18:04 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 02:44 EST, 10 November 2026

Michael Carrick is facing the sack with Manchester United bosses leaning towards installing a new head coach during the international break.

Carrick’s position has become increasingly precarious after United dropped into the relegation zone despite salvaging a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

It left the 45-year-old with just one win from 10 Premier League games this season – United’s worst start since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago.

Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a new frontrunner to replace Carrick. The Argentine is currently in charge of the US national team, but his contract includes a £7million release clause.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, who were both under consideration when United gave Carrick more time to turn the season around following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth last month, could also be in contention.

In the three games since then, Carrick’s side lost at Chelsea, staged a remarkable comeback to beat Roma in the Champions League in midweek and then fought back again to draw with Villa.

Michael Carrick is likely to be sacked from his role as Manchester United manager during the international break

It is understood that United officials have not made a final decision, though there is expectation that there will be a new boss in place after the international break

Although it’s understood that no final decision has been reached over Carrick’s future and insiders say that speculation over his sacking is premature, the expectation within Old Trafford is that a new man will be in charge for the visit to Anfield a week on Sunday.

Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January and the former United midfielder was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

But this season has unravelled alarmingly for United with his three wins in 15 games in all competitions coming at home to newly-promoted Ipswich in the Premier League as well as Sabah of Azerbaijan and Roma in the Champions League.

Asked after Sunday’s chaotic draw with Villa if he would consider quitting, a defiant Carrick said: ‘That's not going to happen.

‘We’re in November. I don’t like this situation and where we are. But we can do something about it. I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it's got to win games.’

Sacking Carrick would leave United searching for their eighth permanent manager or head coach since Ferguson retired 13-and-a-half years ago.

Pochettino was strongly linked with the job when Erik ten Hag was appointed in 2022 and again when the Dutchman was sacked two years later.

The 54-year-old has extensive Premier League experience at Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton and was also in charge at Paris Saint-Germain.

Current US boss - and former Tottenham and Chelsea manager - Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the frontrunner to replace Carrick

Howe was previously seen as the favourite but it’s understood there has been no contact between United and the former Newcastle boss.

It would cost United around £3million in compensation to appoint the 48-year-old under the terms of his departure from St James’s Park in July.

Nagelsmann is available after leaving his role as head coach of the German national team in the summer when they were eliminated from the World Cup following a penalty shootout defeat by Paraguay in the round of 32.

#1541. Sporting Lisbon enter race for Endrick

Roma isn’t giving up on Endrick for January, despite Mourinho publicly closing in on the player.

The 2006-born player, as he told the Brazilian Federation, wants to play more and will do everything he can to advance his career.

An opening for Gasperini? We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks, while the Giallorossi management is working to bring the Real Madrid striker to Trigoria.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport reports, contacts between Roma and Endrick’s entourage are continuing.

#1537. French team: A French international at the heart of a legal standoff

Away from the field, Jean-Philippe Mateta is engaged in a legal standoff with his former lawyer. Pierre-Henri Bovis is demanding 540,000 euros in fees from the French striker. A case which has opposed the two men for several years and which concerns the remuneration of the advisor for his services to the player. According to The Teamit is a “classic lawyer inheritance dispute”. But the versions differ radically: the lawyer’s camp accuses the player of “multiply procedures to avoid paying”while that of Mateta denounces “unfounded procedures”.

It all started in 2018, when Pierre-Henri Bovis took charge of certain personal and professional disputes from Jean-Philippe Mateta. A year later, the two men signed a sporting mandate. The lawyer is then responsible for managing the attacker’s career in exchange for 10% of his income. At this time, the player had just extended his contract for two years with Mainz. But his advisor will not immediately receive remuneration for his services, preferring to wait for a future transfer to receive the amounts due to him.

Loaned to Crystal Palace in 2021, Jean-Philippe Mateta permanently joined the Eagles the following year. But in the meantime, the attacker has changed lawyers. Dismissed in July 2020, Me Bovis was replaced by Me Paul Latouche. It is then that the dispute takes on another dimension. The former advisor still believes he can claim 10% of the remuneration negotiated as part of the player’s contract extension in Mainz, signed in June 2019.

This claim corresponds to the 540,000 euros claimed today by Pierre-Henri Bovis. After several formal notices, the lawyer won his case before the President of the Paris Bar, who ordered the payment of this sum. But the decision was then overturned by the Paris Court of Appeal in 2023. It ruled that the validity of the mandate must first be examined.

Indeed, Jean-Philippe Mateta’s lawyers contest the validity of the document, considering in particular that it does not comply with the required forms. They also claim that he would not have been signed on January 27, 2019, as indicated, but on the following July 27, i.e. after the player’s extension in Mainz. A version contested by Pierre-Henri Bovis, who claims to have transmitted the mandate to the French Football Federation in February 2019. The former lawyer has since taken the matter to court. A hearing is scheduled for spring 2027.

At the same time, Jean-Philippe Mateta initiated criminal proceedings with civil action for forgery. A complaint which was however closed without further action, according to information from The Team. For his part, Pierre-Henri Bovis has registered a temporary mortgage on the French international’s Parisian apartment. The player tried to have this measure lifted, but without success.

#1530. Inside the world of Captain Chaos at Man United: Michael Carrick will not walk away but here's what the players are saying as they fail to respond to his direction, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 02:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 03:22 EST, 10 November 2026

While the Manchester United fans who had gone ahead with a booze boycott of Old Trafford watched in horror as their team teetered on the brink of total collapse and head coach Michael Carrick clung to his job, you couldn't help but think of Lloyd Bridges as Steve McCroskey, the frazzled air traffic control boss in Airplane! 'Looks like I picked the wrong week to quit drinking!'

God knows United have forced their supporters to hit the bottle this season, not least in the past six days when they have handed a two-goal advantage to Roma and Aston Villa (twice) and still managed to salvage a win and a draw.

But this cannot carry on. As cavalier as United like to be, this is not the way to play football.

Coming out swinging every game like a boxer on his last legs is great for entertainment, it's great for the Sky Sports cameras beaming it live and the Amazon Prime documentary makers filming behind the scenes, but it is not evidence of solid preparation on the training pitch.

Nowhere in the UEFA coaching manuals will you find a chapter on routinely conceding the first two goals being a sensible route to success. For all his bluster after a bonkers 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Carrick knows it and his players know it.

'After we concede goals we show character, but if we do this before we can win much more games,' said Matheus Cunha. 'I don't know why, everyone tries to get answers for that. We want to be the best and show that we can come back. We need to show the mentality to do this from the start.'

As Manchester United head coach, Michael Carrick is doing a convincing impersonation of Captain Chaos

Coming out swinging every game like a boxer on his last legs is great for entertainment, but it is not evidence of solid preparation on the training pitch

It isn't just in the last week either. United were a goal down against Atletico Madrid inside the first minute and Como in the second. They were two down to Villa after three minutes and 40 seconds, the earliest that has happened to United in the Premier League era.

This is not a coincidence. It is not bad luck. This is in the mind-set of these Manchester United players, and the game management of Carrick – and that is what should worry Old Trafford bosses the most.

As if being in the relegation zone for the next two weeks after a start of one win from 10 games – the worst since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago – is not bad enough, United don't seem to be playing to a plan. They are not responding to direction. They are reverting to instinct and moments of skill when everything else fails.

Carrick made reference to it when he spoke before this game, admitting that the players are better when they don't think too much.

'Momentum within games, day-to-day, week-to-week, game-to-game, it's huge,' he said at Carrington on Friday. 'I think it's important with your feelings and your emotions to roll with it. Then your memory can click in and you realise, 'Oh yeah, this is what it feels like, this is how it should be', and you start seeing different things.

'It's all got to come together, but feeling, confidence, and that emotion and sometimes not even thinking. You're at your best when you don't think too much and you just trust and play on instinct, and I think we did a lot of that the other night (against Roma).'

The irony is that Carrick was so measured, so composed as a player. Now, as coach, he is doing a convincing impersonation of Captain Chaos. United's games are reminiscent of the high-scoring madness of Erik ten Hag's last full season in charge, devoid of stability or structure.

That is what Carrick's employers need to consider when they sit down to discuss whether he can restore the sanity of his first four months in charge which guided the club towards third place and Champions League qualification.

Now they are third from bottom and will stay in the relegation zone for the duration of the international break. For three minutes on Sunday, Manchester United – the aristocrats of English football – were actually in last place after Sunderland took the lead against Chelsea and Crystal Palace were still goalless with Liverpool.

United don't seem to be playing to a plan or responding to direction - they are reverting to instinct and moments of skill when everything else fails

Carrick's employers need to consider  whether he can restore the sanity of his first four months in charge

That being in 18th place – one below Coventry – is somehow seen as blessed relief from the unrelenting humiliation of this season, says everything about the state of the club.

At the end of a week that marked 40 years since Ferguson's arrival and was celebrated by a dinner with many of his most famous players, it has been quite the fall from grace.

Which brings us back to the fans. They are a loyal bunch and once again serenaded Carrick off the pitch at full-time having spent much of the previous two hours slaughtering the owners, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Protest groups had urged them to boycott buying alcohol at the stadium to hit the Glazer family and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in the pocket. 'Your funeral not ours – sell up now,' read one new banner. 'We don't want a new stadium, we want new owners,' said another.

But they know their football at United. Was it support or just sympathy with a head coach who has done his best in an impossible situation?

Carrick says he won't walk away and they never do. On Remembrance Sunday, he stood there on the touchline with a poppy on his arm and hope in his heart that United could get themselves out of another self-inflicted crisis.

They did. Again. But how much longer can United and Carrick keep winging it, and believe that calm will emerge from the chaos.

#1528. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club showed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

They have buttressed the two areas in which they were already strong by signing Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa, but failed to sign the level-raising forward Mikel Arteta coveted.

In fact, with Gabriel Jesus, Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli departing (as well as Ethan Nwaneri moving on loan), their weakest department is arguably weaker than this time last year. Christos Tzolis, signed for £34m from Club Brugge, is their only attacking purchase.

But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.

This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that.

Crystal Palace have agreed a deal to re-sign Ben Chilwell. The 29-year-old was on loan at Palace last year and deal struck with Strasbourg for him to leave French club and return to the Premier League.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Forgive the personal opinion but this is my favourite deal of the window. Mudryk played some of his best football under Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk. The Spurs head coach has even described Mudryk as “my son”, and has previously tipped him as a future Ballon d’Or winner.

After so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

Iliman Ndiaye has been confirmed as a Manchester City signing. He moves on a five-year deal from Everton with the deal worth £65m.

United would be more likely to bring in another player, probably a left-back rather than a direct replacement, if Zirkzee was to go but time running out on that front.

United had hoped to sell Manuel Ugarte and Zirkzee this summer and were in the market for buyers for Marcus Rashford, but the window could close with all three staying put. Ugarte’s serious knee injury put paid to the Uruguay midfielder leaving and Rashford has been reintergrated in the squad after Barcelona opted against taking up an option to sign him permanently.

Benfica are in talks about loaning Argentina Under-23 forward Claudio Echeverri from Manchester City, It’s likely to be a season long loan with an option to buy if finalised.

Fabio Vieira has completed his move from Arsenal to Hamburg, in a deal believed to be worth about £9m. The Portuguese midfielder has never cut it in the Premier League and it is no surprise that Arsenal have cashed in. They paid more than £30m to sign him from Porto in 2022 but he has never come close to justifying the fee. In truth, it’s one of their worst transfers under Mikel Arteta.

Southampton forward Cameron Archer is on course to sign for Auxerre on a season-long loan.

Archer has been a target for a number of Championship clubs this summer but a deal has been problematic because of his £35,000-a-week wages.

It is understood Southampton have been demanding that his salary be paid in full, which has scared off interested clubs in the second tier.

Chelsea will hold off sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City until they are confident of making at least one signing of their own.

Telegraph Sport understands that Chelsea have already rejected one proposal from City for Fernández during club-to-club talks and are demanding a fee and payment terms that are favourable to them.

Chelsea also have three separate targets of their own as potential deadline signings – Lamine Camara, Manu Kone and one mystery target from the Premier League.

Monaco have already rejected a £38.5m bid from Chelsea for Camara. Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini wants to keep Kone, although negotiations continue. And there is a third target from the Premier League, who is not believed to be Morgan Gibbs-White.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

Monaco have rejected an opening €45m bid from Chelsea for midfielder Lamine Camara. It now remains to be seen if the club increase that offer.

Sunderland have been trying to sign a winger all summer and it appears that they have finally got their man in Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Arsenal had been linked with a move for the 21-year old Belgium international.

Announcing Ansah! ✍️🔗 https://t.co/gweqxOt7aR pic.twitter.com/geZR60ZaTG

The Argentina forward missed three training sessions last week and was not included in Diego Simeone’s squad that travelled to Sevilla last weekend.

Nueva sesión de trabajo del Atleti en Majadahonda esta mañana. Julián Alvarez entrenando con normalidad con el resto del grupo. Objetivo, intentar estar en la lista de convocados para el partido ante el Athletic. Sorloth será baja por lesión. Imagen: @jsancris_ #ClubUria pic.twitter.com/IXAWX7mwrJ

Plenty of chatter about the future of Roma midfielder Manu Koné, who is linked with a move to Chelsea. The France international would be a strong acquisition for Xabi Alonso, but could his potential signing precede an Enzo Fernández exit? All will be revealed in due course...

Of Koné, former France manager Didier Deschamps said: “He’s very effective at winning the ball back, but he shouldn’t be limited to that role of defensive midfielder, because he also makes a difference in his use of the ball.”

Austria centre-back David Affengruber has emerged as potential deadline-day deal for Fulham as they look to bolster Alvaro Arbeloa’s defence.

The Elche player has been in La Liga for two years playing regularly and fits the data model at Craven Cottage.

Fulham are also trying deals for Real Madrid’s Manuel Angel and Eintracht Frankfurt’s Hugo Larsson as midfield options.

Sunderland are expected to complete the signing of centre-back Kevin Danso from Tottenham Hotspur with the player travelling to Wearside last night for the first part of his medical.

The Austria international will initially join on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent for £25m next year.

Danso had made it clear he wanted to leave Tottenham this summer in search of regular first-team football.

Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Nottingham Forest over another loan move for forward Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Frankfurt signed the Frenchman on loan in January and are negotiating a return for Forest’s £26m signing from Rennes.

Oliver Glasner, Forest’s head coach, had been intent on keeping Kalimuendo but it is understood Frankfurt’s strong interest has altered the club’s thinking.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Hull City are close to agreeing a fee of around £7.5m for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

The Wales international has been a long-term target for Hull and negotiations are now approaching a conclusion.

Thomas has been pushing a move through and is expected to leave Stoke after one full season.

As has become the norm this summer Acun Ilicali has posted a cryptic message on X, which has prompted speculation among Hull City fans. The club has been linked with Everton holding midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.

Will Barcola hit the ground running at Anfield? The France winger registered 20 goal contributions in 49 games for Paris St-Germain last season.

A warm welcome from the skipper 😍 pic.twitter.com/95EAqUjYBn

The La Masia graduate secures a permanent move to Germany. Who knows how his career in England would have panned out had Chelsea not recalled him 25 days into his Sunderland loan at the beginning of last season...

Marc Guiu has completed a permanent transfer to Bundesliga side RB Leipzig. Everyone at Chelsea would like to thank Marc for his efforts during his time at the club and wish him every success as he begins the next chapter of his career with RB Leipzig.

What a couple of weeks it has been for Robert Sanchez. He came into this season as Chelsea’s No 1, but after a difficult start to the campaign and Emi Martinez’s arrival, reports suggest he could be moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan. Cesc Fabregas’s Como appears the probable destination.

Trevoh Chalobah, who left Chelsea for Como last month, has taken to his “secondary” Instagram account to post the following picture...

Meanwhile, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, striker flop Nick Woltemade is moving to Juventus on a season-long loan. The club’s record signing from as year ago at £64m is moving to Turin for a £3.5m loan fee with the Serie A squad covering the full cost of his wages.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

A post shared by Ligue 1 McDonald's (@ligue1mcdonalds)

The Leeds wide man has a medical booked with Fiorentina today. He made a handful of appearances for Daniel Farke’s side during pre-season but has not featured since the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

✈️ L'arrivo di Gnonto a Firenze ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/nEFngsyxQP

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Jayden Danns, who broke through three years ago and played in the 2024 League Cup final defeat of Chelsea, is attracting interest from clubs in Europe, who want to take him on loan. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1525. Rio Ferdinand claps back at fans mocking him for celebrating Man United's late equaliser against Aston Villa which left them in the relegation zone

Published: 14:15 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:16 EST, 10 November 2026

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at football fans who criticised his reaction on social media to Manchester United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Former United defender Ferdinand drew criticism when he shared a photo of himself celebrating after the Red Devils' dramatic comeback on Sunday afternoon.

Michael Carrick's side had looked down and out at 4-2 in stoppage time, but late strikes from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu meant they earned a point from the game.

They did, though, remain in the relegation zone – however Ferdinand shared two snaps to his X account following full-time.

The first showed the 48-year-old with his head in his hands, and the second saw him celebrating. He captioned the post: 'From this to THIS!!! Carrick time!!!!!!!!!! Birthday weekend just got (a) tad better in the last 6 minutes…'

Fans though flooded the replies with criticism, questioning why he was 'celebrating a draw' and calling him an 'embarrassment'. Ferdinand, though, has now taken the opportunity to respond.

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at fans who criticised his response to Manchester United's draw with Aston Villa

'Let me just address something,' Ferdinand began on Rio Ferdinand Presents. 'On socials I put a picture up and little comment underneath of me going like that (celebrates).

'That's not me celebrating a point against Aston Villa, by the way, it's me celebrating a moment in a football match. It's what football does to you. It can take over your body, take over your emotions in a moment. That moment isn't the big picture.

'So all of these people saying his standards have dropped and he's celebrating a draw... I'm not celebrating a draw against Villa, I'm celebrating the moment and the fact we actually came back and showed a bit of character.

'It's always about that moment that when you calm down and you go, look where we are in the league, that's terrible, looks how things unfolded in the game, that needs work. But, in the moment, as a football fan, you are allowed to get carried away with it.

'That's what football does. If you don't know that or don't understand it or feel it, you're not a football person, so get out.'

Ferdinand hasn't shied away from criticising his former team-mate Carrick amid United's poor run of form that has left them in 18th in the Premier League table.

United came back from behind to draw 4-4 with Villa having looked down and out in the game

His assessment of Sunday's showing was more tame, with the ex-centre back describing the effort as full of both character and chaos.

He added: 'It's like we need a punch on the nose, or two or three, to start playing. But then, the flip side of it, it's character and ability plays a part in that.

'In the end, we could have won it. But they are giving us fans grey hairs. It's crazy football.'

As thrilling as Man United's fight-back may have been to some fans, manager Carrick was still forced to answer difficult questions at full-time.

Sky Sports' Patrick Davison asked the former captain what he 'expected to happen over the next few weeks' - suggesting a question mark still lingering over his tenure despite comebacks against Roma and Villa.

Carrick's response was understandably thorny, with the manager underlining that he 'probably' would not be walking away from the role.

With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject.

Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week.

#1524. Man Utd’s 2027-28 Championship predicted XI if they’re relegated this season

Manchester United find themselves in the bottom three after their worst-ever start to a Premier League season, and relegation is now a distinct possibility.

United are set to replace Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino in a bid to turn their form around, but there’s no guarantee that it will work.

If United are relegated, most of their big-name players would look to leave, and they would have to reduce the wage bill. We’ve made a predicted Championship XI for United, arranged in a 4-2-3-1 formation.

Despite enduring a poor start to the 2026-27 season, Senne Lammens is still one of the best young goalkeepers in Europe and will not be short on suitors if United are relegated.

Darlow joined United in the summer and is currently the back-up goalkeeper at Old Trafford, but relegation from the Premier League could see him get a promotion on an individual level.

He has made 161 appearances in the second tier and is a two-time Championship winner, lifting the title with Newcastle in 2017 and Leeds in 2025.

Diogo Dalot is the second-longest serving player in the United squad, but has become a much-maligned figure at Old Trafford and is unlikely to stick around for a year in the Championship.

Pochettino’s impending arrival at United could lead to a move for Trippier, who made 114 appearances under the manager during his time at Tottenham.

He is currently playing for Wolves in the Championship and they are targeting an immediate return to the Premier League, but the boyhood United fan would surely jump at the chance to move to Old Trafford.

Maguire celebrates his 34th birthday next year and is widely expected to leave Old Trafford when his contract expires at the end of the season.

But if United are relegated, they could offer him a new deal on reduced terms as his experience and leadership qualities would make him a real asset in the Championship.

The centre-back has made 43 appearances in the second tier and was part of the Hull City side that won promotion via the play-offs in 2015-16.

Heaven joined United from Arsenal in a £1million deal in January 2025 and is one of the lowest-paid players in the squad, taking home a £35,000-per-week salary.

The 20-year-old centre-back initially showed a lot of promise at Old Trafford, but has struggled for form in the opening weeks of this season.

While he would likely be offered the chance to make an immediate return to the Premier League, a season in the Championship and the promise of regular starts could be good for his development.

United retain an interest in Lewis Hall following their tentative enquiries for the Newcastle left-back last summer, but relegation would bring an end to that pursuit.

Harry Amass made 22 appearances in the Championship last season and could finally get a chance in the United team if they drop down to the second tier, but a move for Mitchell feels more likely.

The 27-year-old has entered the final year of his Crystal Palace contract and will be available on a free transfer next summer.

United spent £155million on a midfield overhaul, but relegation to the Championship could see Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans all depart after just one season.

In this scenario, they should pursue a move for Hackney, who won the EFL Championship Player of the Season and the PFA Championship Players’ Player of the Year awards in the 2025/26 campaign.

He left Middlesbrough and completed a £16.5million move to Everton last summer but finds himself behind James Garner and Harrison Armstrong in the pecking order, making just one Premier League start this season.

Dropping back down to the Championship may feel like a backwards step, but playing for United every week is still an appealing prospect.

Kobbie Mainoo has been on United’s books since the age of nine and recently put pen to paper on a contract that ties him to his boyhood club until 2031.

But the midfielder was willing to leave United last year after falling out of the England squad, and a year in the Championship would be detrimental to his chances of playing at Euro 2028.

His departure would hand more opportunities to fellow United academy graduate Tyler Fletcher, who made two first-team appearances last season and won the Denzil Haroun Reserve Team Player of the Year award.

The 19-year-old is also a senior Scotland international and, unlike Mainoo, playing every week in the Championship would help him get selected for Euro 2028.

Lacey has long been heralded as one of the most exciting talents in United’s academy, and he was linked with a loan move to the Championship last summer.

The 19-year-old stayed at Old Trafford and scored in the Carabao Cup against Brighton before coming off the bench to set up the winning goal against Roma in the Champions League.

But he’s yet to start a Premier League game and could be playing every week in the Championship next season, albeit while still remaining at United.

Bruno Fernandes has shown a lot of loyalty towards United during a turbulent period for the club and rejected a £700,000-per-week offer from the Saudi Pro League following their 15th-placed finish in 2024-25.

But relegation to the Championship would be a step too far for the Portugal international, who would have a line of clubs queuing up to secure his signature.

Mount has predominantly been a back-up to Fernandes throughout his time at United, while also struggling with a number of injury issues.

The midfielder was part of the Derby County side that reached the play-off final in 2018-19, and could get his career back on track by playing regular football in the Championship for a season.

He may have to take a pay cut though, with his current wage reported to be around £150,000-per-week.

Despite admitting that he prefers to play at left-back, Dorgu has become increasingly influential in the final third.

The Denmark international registered eight direct goal contributions in 13 appearances under Carrick, including a goal and an assist in his final game.

His pace, physicality and brilliant ball-striking ability would make him the Gareth Bale of the Championship.

United may not be in the relegation zone if Benjamin Sesko had been fully fit this season, but the £74million signing is too good to be playing in the Championship.

Moves for the likes of Jean-Philippe Mateta, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Serhou Guirassy would also be unrealistic, so United may have to shop in the Championship.

Lankshear is currently the best striker in the second tier, having netted 13 goals in 13 league appearances for Middlesbrough this season.

The 21-year-old is seen as a long-term successor to Harry Kane in the England side, and firing United back to the Premier League would be great for his burgeoning reputation.

#1523. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1519. Four ideal signings for Mauricio Pochettino’s Man Utd in January

Mauricio Pochettino is set to take the reins at Manchester United and they’ll be hoping for an immediate boost in their fortunes – but they might have to add to their squad at the next opportunity to give themselves the best chance.

United’s season so far has been a disaster. They’ve gone into the international break sitting in the Premier League’s relegation zone. It’s cost Michael Carrick his job as manager, but quite rightly, the blame is more widespread.

United’s owners, directors and players have all come in for criticism, but if anything’s going to change, it’s probably the latter.

It’d be wrong to expect a mass overhaul in January, a notoriously difficult transfer window to do big business in, but it’d be equally daft to expect United to just sit around and do nothing.

A new manager coming in gives them a chance to bring in new ideas and players to suit those ideas.

So, keeping it semi-realistic, who’d be a good signing for them under Pochettino?

It’s tempting whenever a manager gets a new job to look at who’s at his former clubs that he might like to reunite with.

Ironically in this case, the one familiar player that might most appeal from Tottenham isn’t someone Pochettino worked with at Tottenham – it’s been a while, after all – but at Chelsea instead.

Gallagher was Pochettino’s most-used player during his sole season at Chelsea, playing in 48 of his 51 games in charge.

Sure, United already did a lot of work on their midfield over the summer, but they still seem to be missing runners there. And if there’s one thing Gallagher can do, it’s run. And if there’s one thing Pochettino wants his midfielders to do… you get the picture.

On average, Gallagher has covered 12.2km per 90 minutes when playing in the Premier League this season. It’s the highest average in the squad of anyone with three or more starts.

Pochettino used to rave about Gallagher at Chelsea. Exhibit A, this ringing endorsement in February 2024:

“He is a player with a great commitment to the team. He is always trying to compensate in every situation, in offensive and defensive situations. It’s priceless to have a player like him.

“‘He is in the starting XI nearly every game and one of the captains. For me, he is the type of player that the club need to have.

“He runs, he plays, he fights. He does everything to win. He is a really important player that the coaching staff want to have on the team.”

Gallagher hasn’t exactly been a regular starter for Spurs this season, but he only joined them in January, so he might be tricky to prise away.

But hypothetically, he’d get more of a look in from Pochettino in a midfield where Kobbie Mainoo is a top prospect, but Carlos Baleba has had injury issues, Youri Tielemans hasn’t convinced with his energy and Andrey Santos remains an unknown quantity.

Santos spent the 2023-24 season out on loan away from Chelsea rather than as part of Pochettino’s squad.

Gallagher would add to United’s homegrown quota too, but for a Pochettino team, he wouldn’t just be making up the numbers.

Pochettino got the best out of Luke Shaw when they worked together at Southampton, but Luke Shaw then was different to Luke Shaw now.

Back in those days he was a talented teenage prospect. Nowadays, he’s United’s tired only natural option at left-back. Quite simply, they need to freshen it up.

Pochettino will probably be happy to keep Shaw around as a senior, trustworthy figure. But he’ll be wanting more energy from the full-back positions and that means fresh legs.

Some of Pochettino’s best teams thrived when their full-backs bombed on to offer width while the wingers cut inside. Shaw can’t really do that anymore.

One player who can get up and down the flank is Palace’s Mitchell, who might not be the most inspiring choice but could be the best of what’s available.

Palace’s precarious position, coupled with the fact that Mitchell is out of contract at the end of the season, could make January his ideal time to escape.

His attacking output hasn’t always been cited as a strong point, but he can cover plenty of ground up and down the channel. A Pochettino team don’t necessarily need their full-backs to be the ones getting goals and assists, just to offer support and threatening runs.

Mitchell also has a good record in duels and could offer United more stability in defence, as they desperately need. There might be a signing with a higher ceiling to make, but that’s the kind of thing that might have to wait until the summer.

It’s not just at left-back United need to upgrade. The battle between Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui on the other side is hardly awe-inspiring, but unless they can shift one or the other, finding an upgrade might be a summer job.

At centre-back, though, they might not be able to afford to wait. Getting Harry Maguire back from injury will be a boost when the time comes, but with Lisandro Martinez suffering a sharp downturn in form, a brand new centre-back would help.

We reckon Nottingham Forest’s Murillo would be a pretty smart signing for United. He’s strong and imposing but also good on the ball, which is perfect for Pochettino.

Is he gettable in January, though? Probably not. He signed a new contract in the summer and we know what Forest are like when it comes to selling players. Or stopping them from being sold.

File this one under the dream signing category. Murillo has Premier League experience, plenty of good years still ahead of him and the attributes that Pochettino values highly in his defenders.

Look, we can safely say Pochettino would love to work with Harry Kane again. We know there have been numerous times when United would have loved to sign Harry Kane. It’s just not happening, though, is it?

Ink dry on his new Bayern Munich contract, Kane is off the menu. But a striker is still high on United’s wish list.

By January, Benjamin Sesko will be just about ready to return from injury, but who knows in what state. In his absence, United don’t have great alternatives. Joshua Zirkzee has had enough chances now and not taken them, while Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are probably better out wide.

The summer transfer window is usually the more likely option for big striker moves. United could still do with someone to put them on, though.

The right kind of middle-ground between luxury signing and mere stop-gap could be someone like Borussia Dortmund’s Guirassy.

He’s the same height as Kane at 6’2 and boasts some similar strengths, such as his link-up play and chance conversion.

With eight goals from 14 games this season, including four from four in the Champions League, he’s in solid form. It’s no anomaly, looking at his last few seasons: 22 goals last time out, 38 the season before, 30 in the one before that.

At 30 years old, he’s not necessarily the long-term solution. But Kane is 33 and you’d sign him, wouldn’t you?

Guirassy might be one of the best options out there in terms of value for money.
